claims.text: Early reduction of Pt, Ir, or Ru salts creates a kinetic noble-metal lattice.
The initial noble-metal lattice promotes H2 dissociation and accelerates reduction of adjacent transition-metal salts.
Accelerated reduction of neighboring transition-metal salts produces a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
Spray drying produces near-spherical precursor particles with compositionally uniform distributions of the mixed salts.
The SD-TDR process produces porous, self-supported 3D nanoframeworks assembled from nanoarms with homogeneous elemental distributions.
Coexisting Pt-based fcc and Ru-based hcp domains mediate structural properties and catalytic activity.
Pt, Ir, or Ru salts reduce before Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe salts at temperatures below 300 °C.
Hydrogen atoms generated by dissociative adsorption reduce nearby Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe species.
Reduced Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe integrate into a pre-established noble-metal framework to yield a single-phase solid solution.
Pt–Ru alloys initially retain a Pt-fcc structure.
Secondary heating overcomes an approximately 0.45 eV energy barrier and enables transformation from Pt-fcc to the more stable Ru-hcp phase.
Higher Ru content favors the fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Increasing Ru content and applying secondary heating at 400–500 °C should increase the hcp phase fraction.
A higher hcp fraction should produce a larger electrochemically active surface area.
A higher hcp fraction should enhance methanol-oxidation mass activity and sustained current relative to commercial Pt black, unheated HEA samples, and Pt-rich compositions.
Commercial Johnson Matthey Pt black has a methanol-oxidation mass activity of 170 mA/mgPt and an electrochemically active surface area of 17.59 m2/gPt.
PtNiCoCuRu synthesized at 300 °C without secondary heating is predominantly Pt-based fcc.
The proposed seeded-reduction mechanism applies from 300 to 500 °C when Pt, Ir, or Ru salts provide an effective noble-metal seed under H2.
The mechanism does not apply to NiCoCuFe without an effective noble-metal seed or to formulations relying on Pd, because Pd does not facilitate efficient H2 dissociation.
Controlled fcc-to-hcp transformation is confined to Pt:Ru ratios between 3:1 and 1:4.

contradictions.description: The material is described as a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution, but catalytic mediation is attributed to coexistence of distinct Pt-fcc and Ru-hcp domains. A time-resolved distinction between the initially single-phase state and the final multiphase state is not stated clearly.
